scenario: AITA for making a Facebook post about someone without telling them? | My (22F) best friend (21M) recently went on a 3 month long trip to India to do volunteer work. He helped to build a water pipeline and taught kids in a local school about hygiene and sanitation. He also paid for the whole trip himself, costing over $3000. He is a pretty shy and quiet guy, so he didn’t tell many people about it before he left and I doubt he was going to when he got back if I didn’t do this. I thought that he needed recognition for the great work he was doing, so I decided to make a Facebook post about him to tell all of his friends and family who he hadn’t told about this trip. I did this while he was away, about a week before he got home. Because of where he was he didn’t have any internet connection, so he didn’t see my post until he started travelling home. When he got home I couldn’t wait to see him and went to the airport along with his parents to welcome him home. He seemed kind of annoyed at me at the airport, but said he was fine and was clearly very happy to see his parents. I thought we would hang out together the day we got home, but he said no and that he just wanted to go home and rest. I decided to text him that evening to ask again what was wrong. He told me he was pissed off at me for the Facebook post. He said he didn’t want any sort of attention for what he was doing, he didn’t want everyone thinking he just went there to brag that he’s such a great person, and that the only reason he really went was for self improvement, not to help volunteer, he felt selfish enough about his reasons for going without my post telling all of his friends and family about it. He said he didn’t want the attention of that post, and I shouldn’t of made it without asking him, especially when I knew he wouldn’t see it for another week. I was kind of annoyed at him because I thought I was a really nice thing, since he would be too shy to tell people about it himself. The post was so positive about him, I didn’t say anything bad. AITA for making that post?

message.reasoning:
Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether the action in this scenario is morally acceptable or not. Let me break it down step by step.

First, the situation: The user is a 22-year-old woman whose best friend, a 21-year-old man, went on a three-month trip to India to volunteer. He built a water pipeline, taught kids about hygiene, and paid over $3000 himself. He's shy and quiet, so he didn't tell many people about it before leaving, and the user didn't think he'd tell people upon returning either. She decided to make a Facebook post about him to give him recognition because she thought he deserved it. She did this while he was away, about a week before he came home. He didn't have internet access there, so he didn't see the post until he started traveling home. When he got back, she went to the airport with his parents to welcome him. He seemed annoyed but said he was fine. They didn't hang out that day, and when she texted him that evening, he told her he was pissed off about the post. He felt it was unnecessary attention, that he didn't want people thinking he was bragging, and that his main reason for going was self-improvement, not just volunteering. He felt the post was selfish and that she shouldn't have done it without asking, especially since she knew he wouldn't see it for a week. The user is upset because she thought it was a nice thing to do, especially since he's shy.

So, the question is: Is the user AITA (Are They In The Wrong) for making that Facebook post?

Let me consider the factors here. The user's intention was good—she wanted to recognize her friend for his good work. She thought he was too shy to share it himself, so she took the initiative. However, she didn't ask him first, and he ended up being upset about it.

On one hand, she was trying to do something kind. She saw his efforts and wanted to celebrate them. It's a positive action in that sense. But on the other hand, she didn't respect his privacy or his wishes. He was explicit about not wanting attention, and she went against that by posting without his consent.

I think the key here is consent. Even though her intentions were good, she didn't ask him if he wanted the post made. She assumed he would appreciate it, but he clearly didn't. His reasons for not wanting attention were valid—he felt it was for self-improvement, not to seek accolades. So, by posting without his knowledge, she overstepped.

Additionally, she knew he wouldn't see the post for a week, which means she couldn't get his feedback before posting. That adds another layer because she was making a decision that would affect him without giving him a chance to respond.

So, while her intention was positive, the lack of consent and the disregard for his privacy make the action morally unacceptable. She should have discussed it with him first before posting about his personal experiences.
